purpose: Source citations for the 'Offline diagnostics and the read-only WAL path' section of the SQLite adoption record: the conditions under which a connection reaches the heap-memory WAL-index path hardened by check-in 9a79ca31ff, what a read-only open does and does not prevent, hot-journal behavior on a read-only connection, and which diagnostic strategies exclude the path.
method: Each citation names a function in the official SQLite 3.53.2 amalgamation and the condition read from its body. Line numbers refer to sqlite3.c inside the archive below; the same functions exist in src/wal.c, src/pager.c, src/btree.c, and src/os_unix.c of the source tree. The fix diff was obtained by comparing the wal.c embedded in the 3.53.2 amalgamation against src/wal.c at the fix check-in. Citations are read from source, not executed; no probe was run for this file.

sources.uri_parameter_docs: sqlite3.h comment block 'URI filenames' (immutable, mode=ro, readonly_shm) in the same archive

fix.comment: When using a read-only WAL/SHM, handle a corrupt page size in the WAL file correctly.

diff_summary.change: Adds 'if( !pWal->szPage ) return 0;' after the page-number check, so a frame is treated as invalid when the connection's page size is zero, before walChecksumBytes() is called with pWal->szPage as the byte count.
Relaxes the debug assertion to '(szPage>=512 && szPage<=65536) || szPage==0' so debug builds no longer abort before the new walDecodeFrame() guard runs.

fix.upstream_report_summary: The reporter opened a database through the shell with 'file:...?mode=ro&readonly_shm=1', a -wal file whose header carries page size 0, and a minimal existing -shm file. walBeginShmUnreliable() allocated only the 24-byte frame header and walChecksumBytes() read past it (AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow, a read overrun). The report demonstrates a crash of a read-only process, not a write primitive.

conditions.claim: The hardened function is reached only from walTryBeginRead() when the connection has already marked its shared memory unreliable.
conditions.condition: if( !useWal ){ if( pWal->bShmUnreliable==0 ){ rc = walIndexReadHdr(pWal, pChanged); } ... else if( pWal->bShmUnreliable ){ return walBeginShmUnreliable(pWal, pChanged); } }

conditions.claim: bShmUnreliable is set only when mapping wal-index page 0 returns SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT; the connection then switches to a heap-memory wal-index for the read attempt.
conditions.condition: rc = walIndexPage(pWal, 0, &page0); if( rc!=SQLITE_OK ){ if( rc==SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT ){ assert( pWal->readOnly & WAL_SHM_RDONLY ); pWal->bShmUnreliable = 1; pWal->exclusiveMode = WAL_HEAPMEMORY_MODE; *pChanged = 1; } else { return rc; } }

conditions.claim: On the Unix VFS, SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT is returned only when the -shm file was opened read-only and no other process holds any lock on the DMS byte.
conditions.condition: F_GETLK on UNIX_SHM_DMS; if( lock.l_type==F_UNLCK ){ if( pShmNode->isReadonly ){ pShmNode->isUnlocked = 1; rc = SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT; } else { take EXCLUSIVE DMS lock, truncate -shm, downgrade to SHARED } }

conditions.claim: The -shm file is opened read-only (isReadonly=1) in exactly two cases: the URI parameter readonly_shm=1 skips the read-write open, or the O_RDWR|O_CREAT open fails and a fallback O_RDONLY open succeeds. If both opens fail the result is SQLITE_CANTOPEN, not the hardened path. The database connection's own SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY flag is not consulted.
conditions.condition: if( 0==sqlite3_uri_boolean(pDbFd->zPath, "readonly_shm", 0) ){ hShm = robust_open(zShm, O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_NOFOLLOW, mode); } if( hShm<0 ){ hShm = robust_open(zShm, O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW, mode); if( hShm<0 ){ rc = SQLITE_CANTOPEN; } pShmNode->isReadonly = 1; }

conditions.claim: A read-only -shm mapping is PROT_READ and every successful map returns SQLITE_READONLY, which walIndexPage() records as WAL_SHM_RDONLY. When another process does hold the DMS lock, the shared memory is treated as reliable and read-only rather than unreliable.
conditions.condition: pMem = osMmap(0, nMap, pShmNode->isReadonly ? PROT_READ : PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE, ...); ... if( pShmNode->isReadonly && rc==SQLITE_OK ) rc = SQLITE_READONLY;

conditions.claim: walIndexPage() converts SQLITE_READONLY to SQLITE_OK after setting WAL_SHM_RDONLY, and passes SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT through unchanged.
conditions.condition: else if( (rc&0xff)==SQLITE_READONLY ){ pWal->readOnly |= WAL_SHM_RDONLY; if( rc==SQLITE_READONLY ){ rc = SQLITE_OK; } }

conditions.claim: In the reliable read-only-shm case (WAL_SHM_RDONLY set, bShmUnreliable clear), a malformed wal-index header yields SQLITE_READONLY_RECOVERY instead of running recovery, so this case never reaches the hardened function and never writes.
conditions.condition: if( badHdr ){ if( pWal->bShmUnreliable==0 && (pWal->readOnly & WAL_SHM_RDONLY) ){ if( SQLITE_OK==(rc = walLockShared(pWal, WAL_WRITE_LOCK)) ){ walUnlockShared(pWal, WAL_WRITE_LOCK); rc = SQLITE_READONLY_RECOVERY; } } else { ... walIndexRecover(pWal) ... } }

conditions.claim: In the unreliable case the heap-memory wal-index is built by walIndexRecover(), which reads the -wal file and writes only to heap pages because exclusiveMode is WAL_HEAPMEMORY_MODE (walIndexPage allocates with sqlite3MallocZero and walLockExclusive returns SQLITE_OK without locking). A -wal header with page size 0, non-power-of-two, above SQLITE_MAX_PAGE_SIZE, or below 512 makes recovery jump to 'finished' with a zeroed header, so hdr.szPage stays 0.
conditions.condition: szPage = sqlite3Get4byte(&aBuf[8]); if( (magic&0xFFFFFFFE)!=WAL_MAGIC || szPage&(szPage-1) || szPage>SQLITE_MAX_PAGE_SIZE || szPage<512 ){ goto finished; } ... finished: if( rc==SQLITE_OK ){ walIndexWriteHdr(pWal); ... }

conditions.claim: walIndexTryHdr() accepts a header whose szPage is 0 (it checks only the double-read consistency, isInit, and the header checksum) and derives pWal->szPage = 0 from it.
conditions.condition: if( h1.isInit==0 ) return 1; walChecksumBytes(...); if( aCksum mismatch ) return 1; ... pWal->szPage = (pWal->hdr.szPage&0xfe00) + ((pWal->hdr.szPage&0x0001)<<16);

conditions.claim: In 3.53.2 walBeginShmUnreliable() bounds szPage by assertions only, allocates szPage + WAL_FRAME_HDRSIZE bytes, and calls walDecodeFrame(), which passes pWal->szPage to walChecksumBytes() without a zero check.
conditions.condition: assert( (pWal->szPage & (pWal->szPage-1))==0 ); assert( pWal->szPage>=512 && pWal->szPage<=65536 ); szFrame = pWal->szPage + WAL_FRAME_HDRSIZE; aFrame = sqlite3_malloc64(szFrame); ... walDecodeFrame(pWal, &pgno, &nTruncate, aData, aFrame)

conditions.claim: The WAL is opened only if the pager is not a temp or immutable file and a -wal file exists (or the database header's read version is 2, see C12). A rollback-journal database with no -wal file next to it never constructs a Wal object.
conditions.condition: if( !pPager->tempFile ){ sqlite3OsAccess(pVfs, pPager->zWal, SQLITE_ACCESS_EXISTS, &isWal); if( isWal ){ if( nPage==0 ){ sqlite3OsDelete(pVfs, pPager->zWal, 0); } else { sqlite3PagerOpenWal(pPager, 0); } } else if( journalMode==PAGER_JOURNALMODE_WAL ){ journalMode = PAGER_JOURNALMODE_DELETE; } }

conditions.claim: If the database header read-version byte (offset 19) is 2, the b-tree layer opens the WAL even when no -wal file exists. sqlite3PagerOpenWal() is a no-op for temp or immutable pagers (*pbOpen=1), and sqlite3WalOpen() always requests SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE for the -wal file regardless of the database open flags.
conditions.condition: if( page1[19]==2 && (pBt->btsFlags & BTS_NO_WAL)==0 ){ rc = sqlite3PagerOpenWal(pBt->pPager, &isOpen); } | if( !pPager->tempFile && !pPager->pWal ){ ... pagerOpenWal(pPager) ... } else { *pbOpen = 1; } | flags = (SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE|SQLITE_OPEN_WAL); rc = sqlite3OsOpen(pVfs, zWalName, pRet->pWalFd, flags, &flags); if( rc==SQLITE_OK && flags&SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY ){ pRet->readOnly = WAL_RDONLY; }

conditions.claim: SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY makes the Unix VFS open the database file with O_RDONLY and the pager records readOnly from the VFS output flags. A read-write open that fails for a reason other than EISDIR falls back to O_RDONLY. Creating a journal or -wal in an unwritable directory returns SQLITE_READONLY_DIRECTORY.
conditions.condition: if( isReadonly ) openFlags |= O_RDONLY; ... if( fd<0 ){ if( isNewJrnl && errno==EACCES && osAccess(zName, F_OK) ){ rc = SQLITE_READONLY_DIRECTORY; } else if( errno!=EISDIR && isReadWrite ){ flags |= SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY; ... fd = robust_open(zName, O_RDONLY...) } } | readOnly = (fout&SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY)!=0; ... pPager->readOnly = (u8)readOnly;

conditions.claim: A hot rollback journal on a read-only pager is refused with SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK before any lock upgrade or playback. On a writable pager the same call takes an EXCLUSIVE lock, opens the journal read-write, syncs it, and plays it back into the database file.
conditions.condition: if( !pagerUseWal(pPager) && pPager->eState==PAGER_OPEN ){ ... hasHotJournal(pPager, &bHotJournal); if( bHotJournal ){ if( pPager->readOnly ){ rc = SQLITE_READONLY_ROLLBACK; goto failed; } pagerLockDb(pPager, EXCLUSIVE_LOCK); ... sqlite3OsOpen(pVfs, zJournal, jfd, SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|SQLITE_OPEN_MAIN_JOURNAL, &fout); ... pagerSyncHotJournal(pPager); pager_playback(pPager, !pPager->tempFile); } }

conditions.claim: hasHotJournal() itself only reads: it checks -journal existence, the RESERVED lock, the database page count, and the first journal byte through a read-only open. The one write it can perform, deleting a stale journal when the database has zero pages, requires taking a RESERVED lock and is skipped if the lock is not granted.
conditions.condition: if( nPage==0 && !jrnlOpen ){ if( pagerLockDb(pPager, RESERVED_LOCK)==SQLITE_OK ){ sqlite3OsDelete(pVfs, pPager->zJournal, 0); } } else { f = SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY|SQLITE_OPEN_MAIN_JOURNAL; sqlite3OsOpen(...); sqlite3OsRead(jfd, &first, 1, 0); *pExists = (first!=0); }

conditions.claim: immutable=1 (or SQLITE_IOCAP_IMMUTABLE) forces SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY and routes the pager through the temp-file branch: tempFile=1, eState=PAGER_READER, eLock=EXCLUSIVE_LOCK pretended, noLock=1. Because eState is never PAGER_OPEN the hot-journal block in sqlite3PagerSharedLock() is skipped, and because tempFile is set pagerOpenWalIfPresent() and sqlite3PagerOpenWal() never open a WAL.
conditions.condition: if( (iDc & SQLITE_IOCAP_IMMUTABLE)!=0 || sqlite3_uri_boolean(pPager->zFilename, "immutable", 0) ){ vfsFlags |= SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY; goto act_like_temp_file; } ... act_like_temp_file: tempFile = 1; pPager->eState = PAGER_READER; pPager->eLock = EXCLUSIVE_LOCK; pPager->noLock = 1; readOnly = (vfsFlags&SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY);

conditions.claim: The immutable parameter's documented contract is that the file cannot change even by a higher-privilege process; locking and change detection are disabled and a file that does change can produce incorrect results or SQLITE_CORRUPT.
conditions.condition: When immutable is set, SQLite assumes that the database file cannot be changed, even by a process with higher privilege, and so the database is opened read-only and all locking and change detection is disabled. Caution: Setting the immutable property on a database file that does in fact change can result in incorrect query results and/or SQLITE_CORRUPT errors.

conditions.claim: Checkpointing refuses any connection whose WAL or SHM is read-only. It does not consult the database file's own open flags, so a SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY connection with writable -wal and -shm reaches the checkpoint code at close; its writes to the O_RDONLY database descriptor cannot succeed at the VFS.
conditions.condition: if( pWal->readOnly ) return SQLITE_READONLY; | if( zBuf!=0 && SQLITE_OK==(rc = sqlite3OsLock(pWal->pDbFd, SQLITE_LOCK_EXCLUSIVE)) ){ rc = sqlite3WalCheckpoint(pWal, db, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE, ...); } | if( db && 0==(db->flags & SQLITE_NoCkptOnClose) && SQLITE_OK==databaseIsUnmoved(pPager) ){ a = pTmp; } sqlite3WalClose(pPager->pWal, db, pPager->walSyncFlags, pPager->pageSize, a);

strategy_exclusion.strategy: Production database in rollback-journal mode (DELETE, TRUNCATE, or PERSIST), no -wal file present
strategy_exclusion.basis: C11 and C12: no Wal object is created unless a -wal file exists or the header read version is 2.
strategy_exclusion.residual: A stray -wal file next to a rollback-mode database with nPage>0 is still opened (C11). Hot-journal playback on a writable connection writes (C14).

strategy_exclusion.basis: C16: tempFile=1 disables WAL opening and the hot-journal block; noLock=1 disables locking.
strategy_exclusion.residual: C17: unsafe if any other process writes during the open; WAL content is ignored, so the view can be stale or inconsistent, and a mid-write snapshot can report SQLITE_CORRUPT.

strategy_exclusion.strategy: Open with SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY (mode=ro) on a WAL-mode database
strategy_exclusion.basis: C4 and C12: the read-only flag affects only the database descriptor; -wal and -shm are opened read-write and created when the directory allows, so recovery can write the -shm. When the -shm is unwritable and no other process holds the DMS lock, C3 and C2 put the connection on the hardened path.
strategy_exclusion.residual: Read marks and recovery write the -shm; missing -wal or -shm files are created when the directory is writable (C12, C4).

strategy_exclusion.basis: C4 opens the -shm read-only unconditionally; C3 returns SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT whenever no other process holds the DMS lock, which is the normal state for a single-process tool. This is the reporter's reproduction configuration.
strategy_exclusion.residual: This is the configuration that most reliably enters the hardened path.

strategy_exclusion.strategy: Open normally (read-write) and accept that recovery may write
strategy_exclusion.basis: C3 and C4: with a writable -shm the DMS lock is taken and the shared memory is initialized normally; isReadonly is never set, so SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT cannot be returned. C14: a hot journal is played back.
strategy_exclusion.residual: WAL recovery writes the -shm, hot-journal playback writes the database file and deletes the journal, and close may checkpoint (C18). None of these is side-effect-free.

strategy_exclusion.strategy: Do not open through SQLite; inspect file presence, permissions, and header bytes only
strategy_exclusion.basis: No SQLite pager or WAL code runs. The 100-byte header (magic string, page size at offset 16, read/write versions at offsets 18 and 19) is readable without a library call.
strategy_exclusion.residual: No schema, integrity, or content validation; cannot report on WAL content, journal hotness, or lock state beyond file existence.

limits: Citations are read from source and the upstream report; the hardened path was not exercised here, and the Unix VFS is the only VFS read (Windows shm handling differs in os_win.c). Fossil check-in ancestry and the 3.53.3 containment of 9a79ca31ff are from fix-ancestry.json, not re-established here.
